snippet.textDisplay: Bit of a theater nerd here and here's a look into how they made that jump look seamless: This show uses lighting and shadows to help perform the majority of tricks. Anything that isn't wires (such as when Delphini's actor has to fly toward the end) or a standard magician's trick utilizing practical effects is done by cast members dressed head to toe in black that stay in the non-illuminated parts of the stage further back and help lift the actors and objects in the lighted areas during scenes such as this. If you know what to look for then they get easier to spot (for instance, when Tom jumps and his arms go forward as if he's trying to balance himself, you can see the arm and hand reaching out from the shadows). Those of us in the theater world call them "stage ninjas" due to how they're dressed and how they help pull off feats like this with few in the audience knowing.
